text.en: Wait, what's a TPU? 🤔
text.th: Wait, what's a TPU? 🤔

text.en: TPU stands for Tensor Processing Unit. TPUs are Google's own AI accelerators. They are chips built for one job: the matrix math that neural networks spend most of their time on. Google has been designing them for about ten years, and uses them to train and serve its own models, including Gemini.
text.th: TPU stands for Tensor Processing Unit. TPUs are Google's own AI accelerators. They are chips built for one job: the matrix math that neural networks spend most of their time on. Google has been designing them for about ten years, and uses them to train and serve its own models, including Gemini.

text.en: TPUs are available on Google Cloud, from a single chip up to pods of thousands of chips. They shine when you need a lot of compute, for training or for serving at scale.
text.th: TPUs are available on Google Cloud, from a single chip up to pods of thousands of chips. They shine when you need a lot of compute, for training or for serving at scale.

text.en: The catch has always been software. The TPU stack grew up around TensorFlow and JAX, and PyTorch users had to work harder to get in.
text.th: The catch has always been software. The TPU stack grew up around TensorFlow and JAX, and PyTorch users had to work harder to get in.

text.en: The old way
text.th: The old way

text.en: Until now, running PyTorch on TPUs meant going through PyTorch/XLA (torch_xla). It worked, but it had its quirks. Tensors were lazy (the tensors, not you), so your code didn't always run when you thought it did. Small changes could trigger graph recompilations, and debugging was hard to reason about.
text.th: Until now, running PyTorch on TPUs meant going through PyTorch/XLA (torch_xla). It worked, but it had its quirks. Tensors were lazy (the tensors, not you), so your code didn't always run when you thought it did. Small changes could trigger graph recompilations, and debugging was hard to reason about.

text.en: To make life easier, we built Optimum TPU. It gave Hugging Face models inference and training support on TPUs. Now that TorchTPU brings native support, Optimum TPU is not required anymore to run Hugging Face models with Transformers and Diffusers.

text.en: Enter TorchTPU 🚀
text.th: Enter TorchTPU 🚀

text.en: The extra index gives you the CPU build of torch. Without it, pip pulls the much bigger CUDA build, which you don't need on a TPU.

text.en: Transformers
text.th: Transformers

text.en: Transformers v5 was built around one idea: be the source of truth for model definitions, so they can run anywhere. "Anywhere" now includes TPUs. To load a model on a TPU, pass device_map="tpu". That's it.
text.th: Transformers v5 was built around one idea: be the source of truth for model definitions, so they can run anywhere. "Anywhere" now includes TPUs. To load a model on a TPU, pass device_map="tpu". That's it.

text.en: The model runs in eager mode by default. You can also use torch.compile for better performance, or run it in a distributed setup.
text.th: The model runs in eager mode by default. You can also use torch.compile for better performance, or run it in a distributed setup.

text.en: Images? Videos? Diffusers paints them on TPUs 🎨
text.th: Images? Videos? Diffusers paints them on TPUs 🎨

text.en: TPU is now a first-class device in Diffusers. For prototyping or debugging, eager mode only needs pipe.to("tpu"). For deployment, compiled mode adds one compile call. Your pipelines and code stay the same, and there's no TPU fork to maintain.
text.th: TPU is now a first-class device in Diffusers. For prototyping or debugging, eager mode only needs pipe.to("tpu"). For deployment, compiled mode adds one compile call. Your pipelines and code stay the same, and there's no TPU fork to maintain.

text.en: The first call compiles, and every call after that with the same image size reuses the graph.
text.th: The first call compiles, and every call after that with the same image size reuses the graph.

text.en: Models too big for one chip? Pass a TensorParallelConfig to from_pretrained and the transformer is sharded across chips as it loads, so the full model never has to fit in one place. Many popular pipelines support it out of the box, and the ones that don't are just a tp_plan away. The Diffusers TPU guide has the full recipe.

text.en: We test it so you don't have to 🧪
text.th: We test it so you don't have to 🧪

text.en: We're continuously improving TPU support in transformers by running the library test suite. We are working to add a nightly CI on TPU and make the results available in the (transformers dashboard)[https://huggingface.co/spaces/transformers-community/transformers-ci-dashboard].

text.en: The Transformers CI dashboard, with TPU results next to other accelerators. Work in progress!
text.th: The Transformers CI dashboard, with TPU results next to other accelerators. Work in progress!

body.alt: Transformers CI dashboard with TPU test results next to other accelerators

text.en: It's not all green yet, and we're fine with that. Of the tests that run on TPU, 96.5% pass. Every failure we find becomes a small repro script and an issue on the TorchTPU repo. So far we have reported 34 issues, and 19 are already fixed. Running on TPU also caught a few bugs in Transformers itself, like in StaticCache and the Qwen3 tensor-parallel plans. We fixed those upstream.
